column1: # planning/fidelity/insights.pairing.tsv — which build node answers which mock affordance.
# Four tab-separated columns:  state <TAB> affordance <TAB> node <TAB> citation
# This file declares ONLY the pairing. present, divergent, absent and unclassified are computed by
# scripts/acceptance/mock_fidelity.py from the two artifacts on every run, which is what makes
# `present` earned by measuring rather than asserted. An affordance with no line becomes `absent`,
# which is a finding — deleting a line hides nothing.
# A citation is external and PRE-EXISTING. EVERY ONE OPENS WITH `Dn · `, naming the divergence in
# insights.layers.json this row's finding falls under.
#   node = -            the affordance has no counterpart in the build
#   affordance = +path  a build node with no counterpart in the mock, cited
# THE FACT THAT DECIDES MOST OF THIS FILE: three of the mock's four frames are about the session
# analyst, and this product has no analyst in any form (PRD.md §6 specifies one, nothing in
# app/Sources implements it). So the mock's v-loading is the analyst running, its v-error is the
# analyst falling back, and a third of its v-ideal is the analyst's configuration — none of which
# the build can answer without inventing the subsystem. See D1 and D5.
